Class SmcSensorValues

java.lang.Object
oshi.util.common.platform.mac.SmcSensorValues
@ThreadSafe public final class SmcSensorValues extends Object
Connection-independent interpretation of the values macOS SMC sensor keys report.

These methods take a reading rather than an SMC connection, so the JNA and FFM backends share them and so they can be tested without Mac hardware. Locating the keys themselves is SmcKeyIndex.

  • Field Details

    • MIN_PLAUSIBLE_VOLTAGE

      public static final double MIN_PLAUSIBLE_VOLTAGE
      The lowest reading accepted as a genuine CPU voltage, in volts.

      No CPU core rail runs this low. The lowest confirmed reading is 0.748 V, from VP0C on an M3 Pro, and the nearest neighbour on that machine is 0.864 V.

      What this rejects is a value scaled by the wrong factor: an fpe2 reading treated as volts rather than millivolts yields about 0.0012 V where 1.2 V was meant. That is two orders of magnitude below the floor, and the floor is two orders of magnitude below a real reading, so it sits in an empty band with margin either way.

      Unlike temperature there is no known voltage sentinel: an idle-gated sensor parks its temperature below ambient, but nothing comparable has been observed for the voltage keys. This is a scaling and garbage guard rather than a sentinel filter.

      See Also:

  • Method Details

    • toRpm

      public static int toRpm(double reading)
      Converts a fan speed reading to rpm.

      A reading of zero is preserved rather than discarded. A fan that is stopped genuinely reads zero: on an idle M3 Pro both F0Ac and F1Ac read 0.0 while F0Mn and F0Mx report 1350 and 5349, so the fans are present and readable but not spinning. Dropping those readings would turn two stopped fans into no fans, and Sensors.getFanSpeeds() distinguishes the two: an empty array means no fans were detected, while a zero entry means a fan whose speed is zero or could not be measured.

      Parameters:
      reading - the raw reading
      Returns:
      the speed in rpm, never negative

    • scaleVoltage

      public static double scaleVoltage(double raw, String dataType)
      Converts a voltage reading to volts, according to the units its SMC data type implies.

      An fpe2 value is fourteen integer bits and two fractional bits, so it resolves to a quarter of a unit over a range of 0 to 16383.75. Read as volts that would express a 1.2 V core rail only as 1.00 or 1.25, which is too coarse to be the intent; read as millivolts it resolves to 0.25 mV over 0 to 16.4 V, which is what a voltage sensor wants. Millivolts is the only self-consistent reading, so an fpe2 value is scaled.

      Every other type is already in volts, including the flt that Apple Silicon reports. Scaling from the type rather than from the key name means a key whose encoding differs from the one expected still reads correctly.

      Parameters:
      raw - the decoded reading
      dataType - the key's SMC data type, which may be empty if that read failed
      Returns:
      the reading in volts
